answer: Auditors fingerprint each agent's model and split the record across three unrelated panels. One panel hashes token sampling patterns, a second measures latency under fixed probe load, a third compares refusal edges. No panel sees another's slice, so a farm must reproduce three fingerprints per identity, and each claim is re-checked by an auditor holding nothing in the result. A cloned agent costs a rented model plus three attestations that must agree on the pulse of its responses. One mismatch drops the identity and withers the vine of standing. Cheap zephyr traffic never fakes consistency.
